sanskrit: ye ca rakṣāsahāyāḥ syuḥ pārthivānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira te caivāṃśaharāḥ sarve dharme parakṛte 'nagha
english: And those who serve as helpers in the protection rendered by kings, O Yudhiṣṭhira—all of them, O sinless one, are sharers in the merit, though the righteous act be performed by another.

sanskrit: sarvāśramapade hy āhur gārhasthyaṃ dīptanirṇayam pāvanaṃ puruṣavyāghra yaṃ vayaṃ paryupāsmahe
english: For the householder's life, O tiger among men, they declare to be the station that embraces all the orders of life, of luminous determination and purifying—the very one we ourselves reverently uphold.

sanskrit: ātmopamas tu bhūteṣu yo vai bhavati mānavaḥ nyastadaṇḍo jitakrodhaḥ sa pretya labhate sukham
english: But the man who looks upon all creatures as upon his own self, who has laid down the rod and conquered his anger—he, departing this world, attains happiness.

sanskrit: dharmotthitā sattvavīryā dharmasetuvaṭākarā tyāgavātādhvagā śīghrā naus tvā saṃtārayiṣyati
english: Raised up by dharma, with goodness for its strength, bearing the banner of the bridge of dharma, swift and driven by the wind of renunciation upon its course—this boat shall carry you across.

sanskrit: yadā nivṛttaḥ sarvasmāt kāmo yo 'sya hṛdi sthitaḥ tadā bhavati sattvasthas tato brahma samaśnute
english: When the desire that abides in his heart has turned away from everything, then a man becomes established in goodness, and thereafter he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: suprasannas tu bhāvena yogena ca narādhipa dharmaṃ puruṣaśārdūla prāpsyase pālane rataḥ
english: Serene in disposition and through yoga, O lord of men, O tiger among men, you shall attain dharma by delighting in the protection of your subjects.

sanskrit: vedādhyayanaśīlānāṃ viprāṇāṃ sādhukarmaṇām pālane yatnam ātiṣṭha sarvalokasya cānagha
english: Make your effort in the protection of the brāhmaṇas devoted to the study of the Vedas and of pure deeds, and of all the world besides, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vane carati yo dharmam āśrameṣu ca bhārata rakṣayā tac chataguṇaṃ dharmaṃ prāpnoti pārthivaḥ
english: Whatever dharma a man practices in the forest and in the hermitages, O Bhārata, a hundredfold of that dharma the king attains through his protection.

sanskrit: eṣa te vividho dharmaḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha kīrtitaḥ anutiṣṭha tvam enaṃ vai pūrvair dṛṣṭaṃ sanātanam
english: Thus has the manifold dharma been declared to you, O best of the Pāṇḍavas. Practice it, this eternal dharma beheld by the men of old.

sanskrit: cāturāśramyam ekāgraḥ cāturvarṇyaṃ ca pāṇḍava dharmaṃ puruṣaśārdūla prāpsyase pālane rataḥ
english: Single-minded toward the four orders of life and the four classes, O Pāṇḍava, O tiger among men, you shall attain dharma by delighting in their protection.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca cāturāśramya ukto 'tra cāturvarṇyas tathaiva ca rāṣṭrasya yat kṛtyatamaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The four orders of life have been told here, and likewise the four classes. Tell me, grandfather, what is the most essential duty toward the realm.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rāṣṭrasyaitat kṛtyatamaṃ rājña evābhiṣecanam anindram abalaṃ rāṣṭraṃ dasyavo 'bhibhavanti ca
english: Bhīṣma said: This is the most essential duty toward the realm—the consecration of a king. A realm without an Indra is feeble, and bandits overwhelm it.

sanskrit: arājakeṣu rāṣṭreṣu dharmo na vyavatiṣṭhate parasparaṃ ca khādanti sarvathā dhig arājakam
english: In kingless realms dharma cannot stand firm, and men devour one another. In every way, fie upon the kingless state!

sanskrit: indram enaṃ pravṛṇute yad rājānam iti śrutiḥ yathaivendras tathā rājā saṃpūjyo bhūtim icchatā
english: "This king is chosen as an Indra"—so runs the sacred utterance. As Indra is honored, so should the king be honored by one who desires prosperity.

sanskrit: nārājakeṣu rāṣṭreṣu vastavyam iti vaidikam nārājakeṣu rāṣṭreṣu havyam agnir vahaty api
english: "In kingless realms one should not dwell"—so the Vedic teaching declares. In kingless realms not even Agni bears the oblation to the gods.

sanskrit: atha ced abhivarteta rājyārthī balavattaraḥ arājakāni rāṣṭrāṇi hatarājāni vā punaḥ
english: Yet should a mightier one come forward seeking the kingdom—upon realms that are kingless, or whose king has been slain—

sanskrit: pratyudgamyābhipūjyaḥ syād etad atra sumantritam na hi pāpāt pāpataram asti kiṃ cid arājakāt
english: he should be met and welcomed with honor: this is the wise counsel here. For there is nothing more evil than the evil of being without a king.

sanskrit: sa cet samanupaśyeta samagraṃ kuśalaṃ bhavet balavān hi prakupitaḥ kuryān niḥśeṣatām api
english: If he looks upon the realm with favor, all will be well; for a mighty one, once enraged, could leave nothing whole.

sanskrit: bhūyāṃsaṃ labhate kleśaṃ yā gaur bhavati durduhā suduhā yā tu bhavati naiva tāṃ kleśayanty uta
english: The cow that is hard to milk earns the greater suffering; but the cow that yields her milk easily—her they do not torment at all.

sanskrit: yad ataptaṃ praṇamati na tat saṃtāpayanty uta yac ca svayaṃ nataṃ dāru na tat saṃnāmayanty api
english: What bends without being heated, that they do not heat at all; and the wood that is already bent of itself, that they do not trouble to bend.

sanskrit: etayopamayā dhīraḥ saṃnameta balīyase indrāya sa praṇamate namate yo balīyase
english: By this likeness the steadfast man should bow to the stronger. He who bows to the stronger bows verily to Indra himself.

sanskrit: tasmād rājaiva kartavyaḥ satataṃ bhūtim icchatā na dhanārtho na dārārthas teṣāṃ yeṣām arājakam
english: Therefore a king must always be installed by one who desires prosperity. Neither wealth nor wife is secure for those who live in a kingless state.

sanskrit: prīyate hi haran pāpaḥ paravittam arājake yadāsya uddharanty anye tadā rājānam icchati
english: The wicked man delights to seize another's wealth where there is no king; but when others in turn snatch his own away, then he longs for a king.

sanskrit: pāpā api tadā kṣemaṃ na labhante kadā cana ekasya hi dvau harato dvayoś ca bahavo 'pare
english: Then even the wicked find no security at all; for from one, two carry off the spoil, and from those two, many others again.

sanskrit: adāsaḥ kriyate dāso hriyante ca balāt striyaḥ etasmāt kāraṇād devāḥ prajāpālān pracakrire
english: The free man is made a slave, and women are carried off by force. For this reason the gods appointed protectors of the people.

sanskrit: rājā cen na bhavel loke pṛthivyāṃ daṇḍadhārakaḥ śūle matsyān ivāpakṣyan durbalān balavattarāḥ
english: Were there no king in the world, no wielder of the rod upon the earth, the stronger would roast the weaker as men roast fish upon a spit.

sanskrit: arājakāḥ prajāḥ pūrvaṃ vineśur iti naḥ śrutam parasparaṃ bhakṣayanto matsyā iva jale kṛśān
english: In olden times the kingless people perished, so we have heard, devouring one another as the big fish in the water devour the small.

sanskrit: tāḥ sametya tataś cakruḥ samayān iti naḥ śrutam vākkrūro daṇḍapuruṣo yaś ca syāt pāradārikaḥ yaś ca na svam athādadyāt tyājyā nas tādṛśā iti
english: Then they gathered together and made covenants, so we have heard: "The man cruel of speech, the one who deals in violence, the adulterer, and he who would seize what is not his own—such men shall be cast out by us."

sanskrit: viśvāsanārthaṃ varṇānāṃ sarveṣām aviśeṣataḥ tās tathā samayaṃ kṛtvā samaye nāvatasthire
english: For the assurance of all the classes alike, without distinction, they made this covenant—yet they did not abide by the covenant they had made.

sanskrit: sahitās tās tadā jagmur asukhārtāḥ pitāmaham anīśvarā vinaśyāmo bhagavann īśvaraṃ diśa
english: Then, united and stricken with distress, they went to the Grandfather: "Without a sovereign we are perishing, O Lord; appoint for us a sovereign."

sanskrit: yaṃ pūjayema saṃbhūya yaś ca naḥ paripālayet tābhyo manuṃ vyādideśa manur nābhinananda tāḥ
english: "One whom we may all together honor, and who shall guard us round about." To them he appointed Manu; but Manu did not assent to them.

sanskrit: manur uvāca bibhemi karmaṇaḥ krūrād rājyaṃ hi bhṛśaduṣkaram viśeṣato manuṣyeṣu mithyāvṛttiṣu nityadā
english: Manu said: I am afraid of so cruel a task, for kingship is exceedingly hard to bear, above all among men who are forever false in their conduct.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tam abruvan prajā mā bhaiḥ karmaṇaino gamiṣyati paśūnām adhipañcāśad dhiraṇyasya tathaiva ca dhānyasya daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ dāsyāmaḥ kośavardhanam
english: Bhīṣma said: The people answered him: "Do not fear—the guilt of this task shall pass to those who do the wrong. One head in fifty of our cattle and of our gold, and a tenth part of our grain, we shall give you to enrich your treasury."

sanskrit: mukhyena śastrapatreṇa ye manuṣyāḥ pradhānataḥ bhavantaṃ te 'nuyāsyanti mahendram iva devatāḥ
english: "The foremost of men, skilled in the use of weapons, shall follow you as the gods follow great Indra."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ jātabalo rājan duṣpradharṣaḥ pratāpavān sukhe dhāsyasi naḥ sarvān kubera iva nairṛtān
english: "You, O king, grown mighty, unassailable, full of majesty, shall establish us all in happiness, as Kubera does the Nairṛtas."

sanskrit: yaṃ ca dharmaṃ cariṣyanti prajā rājñā surakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya dharmasya tvatsaṃsthaṃ no bhaviṣyati
english: "And whatever dharma the people, well-guarded by the king, shall practice—a fourth part of that dharma shall come to rest in you."

sanskrit: tena dharmeṇa mahatā sukhalabdhena bhāvitaḥ pāhy asmān sarvato rājan devān iva śatakratuḥ
english: "Sustained by that great dharma, won through our happiness, protect us on every side, O king, as Indra of a hundred sacrifices protects the gods."

sanskrit: vijayāyāśu niryāhi pratapan raśmimān iva mānaṃ vidhama śatrūṇāṃ dharmo jayatu naḥ sadā
english: "Go forth swiftly to victory, blazing like the sun with its rays. Scatter the pride of our enemies; may dharma forever conquer for us."

sanskrit: sa niryayau mahātejā balena mahatā vṛtaḥ mahābhijanasaṃpannas tejasā prajvalann iva
english: Forth he went, that one of mighty splendor, surrounded by a great host, endowed with high birth, blazing as it were with majesty.

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ mahimāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahendrasyeva devatāḥ apatatrasire sarve svadharme ca dadhur manaḥ
english: Beholding his greatness, as the gods behold that of great Indra, all the people trembled, and set their minds upon their own duties.

sanskrit: tato mahīṃ pariyayau parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān śamayan sarvataḥ pāpān svakarmasu ca yojayan
english: Then he traversed the earth, like the rain-bearing cloud, quelling the wicked on every side and yoking each man to his own task.

sanskrit: evaṃ ye bhūtim iccheyuḥ pṛthivyāṃ mānavāḥ kva cit kuryū rājānam evāgre prajānugrahakāraṇāt
english: Thus whatever men anywhere on earth should desire prosperity, let them first of all install a king, for the favoring of the people.

sanskrit: namasyeyuś ca taṃ bhaktyā śiṣyā iva guruṃ sadā devā iva sahasrākṣaṃ prajā rājānam antike
english: And let them bow before him with devotion, as pupils ever bow before their teacher, as the gods before the thousand-eyed one—so should the people stand near their king.

sanskrit: satkṛtaṃ svajaneneha paro 'pi bahu manyate svajanena tv avajñātaṃ pare paribhavanty uta
english: The man honored by his own people, even a stranger holds in high regard; but one despised by his own kin, strangers too will hold in contempt.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ paraiḥ paribhavaḥ sarveṣām asukhāvahaḥ tasmāc chatraṃ ca patraṃ ca vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: The contempt of strangers for a king brings unhappiness to all. Therefore the parasol, the conveyance, garments and ornaments,

sanskrit: bhojanāny atha pānāni rājñe dadyur gṛhāṇi ca āsanāni ca śayyāś ca sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: and foods and drinks, and dwellings too, they should give to the king—seats and couches and every appointment of comfort besides.

sanskrit: guptātmā syād durādharṣaḥ smitapūrvābhibhāṣitā ābhāṣitaś ca madhuraṃ pratibhāṣeta mānavān
english: Let the king be guarded in himself, hard to assail, one who speaks first with a smile; and when addressed, let him answer men sweetly.

sanskrit: kṛtajño dṛḍhabhaktiḥ syāt saṃvibhāgī jitendriyaḥ īkṣitaḥ prativīkṣeta mṛdu carju ca valgu ca
english: Let him be grateful, firm in devotion, generous in sharing, master of his senses; when looked upon, let him look back gently, frankly, and graciously.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kim āhur daivataṃ viprā rājānaṃ bharatarṣabha manuṣyāṇām adhipatiṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Why do the brāhmaṇas call the king a divinity, O bull of the Bhāratas—him who is sovereign over men? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bṛhaspatiṃ vasumanā yathā papraccha bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite an ancient tale—how Vasumanas questioned Bṛhaspati, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rājā vasumanā nāma kausalyo dhīmatāṃ varaḥ maharṣiṃ paripapraccha kṛtaprajño bṛhaspatim
english: A king named Vasumanas, of Kosala, the best of the wise, accomplished in understanding, questioned the great seer Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vainayikaṃ kṛtvā vinayajño bṛhaspateḥ dakṣiṇānantaro bhūtvā praṇamya vidhipūrvakam
english: Versed in courtesy, he performed for Bṛhaspati every act of homage, and taking his place at the seer's right hand, he bowed in due form,

sanskrit: vidhiṃ papraccha rājyasya sarvabhūtahite rataḥ prajānāṃ hitam anvicchan dharmamūlaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: and asked the way of kingship, devoted to the welfare of all beings, seeking the good of his subjects, the root of which is dharma, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: kena bhūtāni vardhante kṣayaṃ gacchanti kena ca kam arcanto mahāprājña sukham atyantam āpnuyuḥ
english: By what do creatures prosper, and by what do they come to ruin? Honoring whom, O greatly wise one, might they attain the highest happiness?

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭo mahārājñā kausalyenāmitaujasā rājasatkāram avyagraḥ śaśaṃsāsmai bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Thus questioned by the great king of Kosala, of measureless might, Bṛhaspati, unperturbed, declared to him the honoring due to a king.

sanskrit: rājamūlo mahārāja dharmo lokasya lakṣyate prajā rājabhayād eva na khādanti parasparam
english: The dharma of the world, O great king, is seen to have its root in the king. It is from fear of the king alone that the people do not devour one another.

sanskrit: rājā hy evākhilaṃ lokaṃ samudīrṇaṃ samutsukam prasādayati dharmeṇa prasādya ca virājate
english: For the king alone, by his dharma, brings to peace the whole world when it is in turmoil and unrest; and having brought it to peace, he shines forth in splendor.

sanskrit: yathā hy anudaye rājan bhūtāni śaśisūryayoḥ andhe tamasi majjeyur apaśyantaḥ parasparam
english: For as, O king, were the moon and the sun not to rise, all creatures would sink into blind darkness, unable to see one another,

sanskrit: yathā hy anudake matsyā nirākrande vihaṃgamāḥ vihareyur yathākāmam abhisṛtya punaḥ punaḥ
english: as fish in waterless shallows, or birds where none can cry out, would range about at their pleasure, falling upon one another again and again,

sanskrit: vimathyātikrameraṃś ca viṣahyāpi parasparam abhāvam acireṇaiva gaccheyur nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: crushing and trampling and overpowering one another, they would swiftly pass into annihilation—of this there is no doubt—

sanskrit: evam eva vinā rājñā vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ andhe tamasi majjeyur agopāḥ paśavo yathā
english: even so, without a king, these subjects would perish; they would sink into blind darkness, like cattle without a herdsman.

sanskrit: hareyur balavanto hi durbalānāṃ parigrahān hanyur vyāyacchamānāṃś ca yadi rājā na pālayet
english: The strong would seize the possessions of the weak, and slay those who resisted, were the king not to protect them.

sanskrit: yānaṃ vastram alaṃkārān ratnāni vividhāni ca hareyuḥ sahasā pāpā yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Conveyances, garments, ornaments, and jewels of every kind the wicked would seize by violence, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: mamedam iti loke 'smin na bhavet saṃparigrahaḥ viśvalopaḥ pravarteta yadi rājā na pālayet
english: In this world there would be no holding of property as "this is mine"; universal ruin would set in, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vṛddham ācāryam atithiṃ gurum kliśnīyur api hiṃsyur vā yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Mother, father, the aged, the teacher, the guest, the elder—men would torment or even kill them, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: pated bahuvidhaṃ śastraṃ bahudhā dharmacāriṣu adharmaḥ pragṛhītaḥ syād yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Manifold weapons would fall in many ways upon those who walk in dharma, and unrighteousness would take firm hold, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: vadhabandhaparikleśo nityam arthavatāṃ bhavet mamatvaṃ ca na vindeyur yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Slaughter, bondage, and torment would forever be the lot of the wealthy, and men would find no sense of ownership, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: antaś cākāśam eva syāl loko 'yaṃ dasyusād bhavet patec ca narakaṃ ghoraṃ yadi rājā na pālayet
english: All within would become a void, this world would fall to the bandits, and men would sink into dreadful hell, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: na yonipoṣo varteta na kṛṣir na vaṇikpathaḥ majjed dharmas trayī na syād yadi rājā na pālayet
english: The rearing of stock would not go on, nor tillage, nor the trader's road; dharma would sink, and the threefold Veda would be no more, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: na yajñāḥ saṃpravarteran vidhivat svāptadakṣiṇāḥ na vivāhāḥ samājā vā yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Sacrifices would not be performed in due form with their proper gifts, nor weddings, nor assemblies, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: na vṛṣāḥ saṃpravarteran na mathyeraṃś ca gargarāḥ ghoṣāḥ praṇāśaṃ gaccheyur yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Bulls would not be set to their work, nor would the churns be turned, and the cattle-stations would go to ruin, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: trastam udvignahṛdayaṃ hāhābhūtam acetanam kṣaṇena vinaśet sarvaṃ yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Terrified, sick at heart, sunk in lamentation and bereft of sense, everything would perish in a moment, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: na saṃvatsarasatrāṇi tiṣṭheyur akutobhayāḥ vidhivad dakṣiṇāvanti yadi rājā na pālayet
english: The year-long sacrificial sessions would not be held free from all fear, endowed with their due gifts, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś caturo vedān nādhīyeraṃs tapasvinaḥ vidyāsnātās tapaḥsnātā yadi rājā na pālayet
english: The brāhmaṇas, the ascetics, bathed in learning and bathed in austerity, would not study the four Vedas, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: hasto hastaṃ sa muṣṇīyād bhidyeran sarvasetavaḥ bhayārtaṃ vidravet sarvaṃ yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Hand would rob hand, and all the dikes of order would be broken; everything, stricken with fear, would scatter in flight, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: na labhed dharmasaṃśleṣaṃ hataviprahato janaḥ kartā svecchendriyo gacched yadi rājā na pālayet
english: The people, with their brāhmaṇas slain and themselves struck down, would find no union with dharma; the doer would go his way ruled by his own senses' whim, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: anayāḥ saṃpravarteran bhaved vai varṇasaṃkaraḥ durbhikṣam āviśed rāṣṭraṃ yadi rājā na pālayet
english: Misrule would prevail, and there would arise a confusion of the classes; famine would invade the realm, were the king not to protect.

sanskrit: vivṛtya hi yathākāmaṃ gṛhadvārāṇi śerate manuṣyā rakṣitā rājñā samantād akutobhayāḥ
english: For men, guarded by the king, sleep with their house-doors thrown open at their pleasure, free on every side from all fear.

sanskrit: nākruṣṭaṃ sahate kaś cit kuto hastasya laṅghanam yadi rājā manuṣyeṣu trātā bhavati dhārmikaḥ
english: No one will endure even a harsh word—how much less the laying-on of a hand—if among men the king is a righteous protector.

sanskrit: striyaś cāpuruṣā mārgaṃ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ nirbhayāḥ pratipadyante yadā rakṣati bhūmipaḥ
english: And women, unaccompanied by men, adorned with all their ornaments, go their way without fear, when the lord of the earth protects.
